context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: The query returns every memory and every associated user with no authentication or ownership check, so any caller can read all Personal Data. Require authentication on the route and scope the query to the authenticated Data Principal, never to an ID from the path or body. Replace the unscoped call with something like: `const memories = await MemoryModel.findAll({ where: { userId: req.user.id }, include: [{ model: UserModel, attributes: ['id', 'name'] }] })`, where `req.user` comes from verified auth middleware. Only return other users' records when the caller holds an explicitly authorised role (e.g. an admin check on `req.user.role`), and then log that access. Restrict included UserModel attributes to the minimum needed, excluding email, password hash, and other sensitive fields. Apply the same authentication and ownership or role check to every HTTP method on this route, including any PUT, PATCH, and DELETE handlers that touch these memories. Verify with tests that an unauthenticated request gets 401, a user requesting another user's memories gets 403 or an empty result, and the owner gets only their own records.
